correctness.rationale: The weighted quadratic plus star TV objective is strictly convex. On each strict fusion pattern S its differential averages the hub and fused leaves with masses m, while all unfused leaves have identity differential. In hub-relative edge coordinates the induced weighted l1 norm is the largest column sum, namely the larger of the identity-column contribution and all fused-leaf mass fractions multiplied by exterior weight sums divided by their input edge weights. For each i in S positivity bounds this by the singleton-S={i} coefficient; strict complementary KKT witnesses realize all faces, including singleton and unfused, and attain ratios at finite distances. Piecewise affine continuity gives the global upper bound across regions. The all-dimensional proof is supplemented by 810 exact-rational face cases, 4050 exact KKT pairs, and 700 independently solved random two-input numerical checks. Boundaries: k>=1, every mass/weight/penalty positive, real data, fixed parameters.

value.rationale: The invariant is the sharp two-signal perturbation stability of widely used graph total-variation denoising. It yields structural thresholds not reducible to an individual-signal TV descent statement: every positive edge reweighting fails for >=4 leaves under equal masses; changing only the hub fidelity mass can restore contractivity, with exact threshold; every strictly positive penalty yields the same global instability even arbitrarily near the identity penalty limit. These are precise motivated stability facts of potential use in network denoiser error propagation.
